title: Maybank Marathon 2026 Review: Indonesia's Only Elite Label Race, in Bali
seo_title: Maybank Marathon 2026 Review | Bali Boston Qualifier
meta_description: Maybank Marathon 2026 review: August 23 in Gianyar, Bali -- Indonesia's only World Athletics Elite Label race, a Boston qualifier since 2013.
dek: Set for 23 August 2026 at the Bali United Training Center in Gianyar, this is Indonesia's only World Athletics Elite Label road race and a Boston Marathon qualifier since 2013 -- a 4:30am start through rice paddies and Balinese villages, with registration already closed.
verdict: The Maybank Marathon has built a genuine reputation over more than a decade: it's Indonesia's only World Athletics 'Elite Label' road race, has been in the Boston Marathon qualifying directory since 2013, and draws repeat runner praise for its village-and-rice-paddy course with gamelan orchestras and flower-petal-scattering schoolchildren along the route. A pre-dawn 4:30am start is a deliberate hedge against Bali's heat and humidity, though some editions have introduced hillier reroutes that participants found genuinely tough. Registration for 2026 closed back in February, so this is one to plan a full year ahead for -- not a race you can decide to enter on short notice.

sections.heading: Indonesia's Only Elite Label Race
paragraphs: The Maybank Marathon is Indonesia's only World Athletics 'Elite Label' road race, and has been listed in the Boston Marathon qualifying directory since 2013 -- a level of certification and organisational rigor that few Southeast Asian marathons can claim. [1] It's held at the Bali United Training Center in Gianyar Regency, on the island's cultural heartland rather than its beach resorts.

sections.heading: A 4:30am Start Through Rice Paddies and Villages
paragraphs: The marathon starts around 4:30am to let runners catch the sunrise and get through the bulk of the distance before humidity builds. [1] The course winds through Balinese villages, rice paddies and rural roads in Gianyar Regency; earlier full-marathon editions started near Bali Safari Park before the first 10km along a dual carriageway toward Sanur. Route support includes marshals in traditional Balinese dress and gamelan orchestras -- a signature feature that repeat participants specifically call out.

sections.heading: What Runners Actually Say
paragraphs: Feedback on independent race-review sites is consistently strong. One MarathonGuide.com reviewer wrote, "I have run over 30 marathons and this ranks as one of the best," [2] and another described "enthusiastic schoolchildren and cheering villagers... with gamelan orchestras playing and even girls scattering flower petals." [2] A 2017 Takbo.ph race recap was blunter about conditions: "The sun can be scorching but the wind was cool." [3] A separate blog gave the 2014 edition 4.6 out of 5. [4]

sections.heading: Watch for Hillier Reroutes and Heat
paragraphs: Not every edition has been uniformly easy. A 2017 participant recap on some rerouted sections noted "there were plenty of instances where runners would rather walk than run the uphill portion." [3] And despite the early start, organisers themselves have publicly acknowledged Bali's hot, humid conditions when discussing race planning -- August in Gianyar typically runs 22-29°C with moderate humidity, so heat management still matters even with sunrise timing.

sections.heading: Registration Is Already Closed for 2026
paragraphs: Registration for the 2026 edition closed on 22 February 2026, well ahead of the August race date -- and slots reportedly sell out fast each year. [1] This isn't a race you can decide to run on a whim; if the 2027 edition follows the same pattern, plan to register in the preceding winter or early spring.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want one of Southeast Asia's most credentialed and best-reviewed marathons -- Boston-qualifying, Elite Label certified, and genuinely praised by repeat finishers for its cultural atmosphere -- the Maybank Marathon on 23 August 2026 earns its reputation. Just note that 2026 registration has already closed, so this year's edition is one to watch rather than enter, with 2027 registration worth marking on a calendar early.
